records.activeValue: On 23 June 2021, CFI-G produced the first observed steady spherical cool diffusion flames of a gaseous fuel aboard the ISS. After more than 150 hot diffusion flames burned between January and June 2021 without transitioning, three tests at n-butane diluted with nitrogen, 40% oxygen in nitrogen, and 2 atm showed hot flames extinguish by radiative heat loss, a ~1 s dark period, then residual burner heat re-igniting the fuel as a steady spherical cool flame much smaller than the hot flame. Cool flames burn at 600–1000 K, far cooler than the 1100–2200 K of typical hot flames.
